note: Landmark structures (ART-L, WAR.md "Living regions"). pieces[]: one pre-built structure each (footprint in tiles, front = +y), states intact (as the season finds it: 60% hp, gates shut, weathered), damaged, ruined (a rubble footprint: slow x2, cover, no function) and restored (the restore rule done: fresh, gates iron-bound, banners); hp = WAR.md where it names one, else the nearest town piece (the sim owns hp). objects[]: one sprite per piece state, fields as public/war/buildings (anchor = foot, tileOrigin = px of the top vertex of the footprint's north tile, basePx = (fw + fh) x 16). <id>-x / <id>-y: the piece along that axis; segments (segmentM) join end to end in every state. kits[]: the labyrinth wall, 16 frames by neighbour mask (+x 1, +y 2, -x 4, -y 8) per state, tileOrigin = the tile top vertex in each frame. landmarks[]: the layout of each landmark in tiles from its NW corner ([piece, x, y]; @id = a build-mode piece from public/war/buildings or a town piece), for region authors and the mock-ups. Colours = tiles.json palette + objects.json palette + palette.

pieces.note: the keep (6 x 6, 8000 hp): a cyclopean tower-house, a flat roof terrace (Drakon perches here in P2) behind a parapet, a roofed stair-house
8 m of the curtain, 2 tiles deep: giant cyclopean blocks, the walk at 7 m behind a 1.2 m parapet; segments join end to end in every state
8 m of the curtain, 2 tiles deep: giant cyclopean blocks, the walk at 7 m behind a 1.2 m parapet; segments join end to end in every state
a curtain tower (6 of them), 6 m square, a tiled roof over its fighting chamber; joins the curtain at walk height
the twin gatehouse: two towers flanking a 4 m passage under a giant lintel, the leaves on the outer (+y) face, a walk between the towers at 7 m
the twin gatehouse: two towers flanking a 4 m passage under a giant lintel, the leaves on the outer (+y) face, a walk between the towers at 7 m
the bone pit (dragonbone node): a low ring of rough stones round a dark pit heaped with old bones, ribs and a drake skull
a one-storey mudbrick house, flat roof with a lip, palm-trunk beam ends, a little roof room
a two-storey mudbrick house on a stone footing, a roof terrace behind a parapet, a stair up its side
the palace (keep, 6000 hp): a stone podium, a mudbrick hall behind a Greek portico of six red-shafted columns (Alexander's), a corner tower, flat roofs
the temple of Ammon (the oracle): an Egyptian pylon of battered limestone towers at the front, a flat-roofed hall with a cavetto cornice behind
the half-sunk temple of Achelous (4 x 4, the sanctum): a peristyle sunk 1.4 m in the mud, its roof half fallen even intact
the colonnade wall: 4 m of stylobate, two columns and the architrave, joining end to end
the colonnade wall: 4 m of stylobate, two columns and the architrave, joining end to end
a river shrine: a little distyle naiskos on a podium, a gable roof
the stone jetty: big slabs on rough piers, mooring bollards
a causeway tile between islands (a ford): big flat stones set in the shallows; lay tile by tile
the river god's spring: a rock basin of dark water under a stele with a horned head spout
the great temple (8 x 8, 12000 hp): a Doric peripteros of 6 x 6 columns on a three-step crepidoma, a painted frieze, a tiled gable
the titan arena: a round of stepped stone seats (20 m) round a sand floor, an arched outer wall, the entrance to +y
the omphalos: the navel stone of the world, an egg of grey stone under a carved net of fillets, on a stepped plinth
a ramp gatehouse (4 of them): the Lion Gate between two square towers at the top of a ramp; the holder's stone gate once restored
a ramp gatehouse (4 of them): the Lion Gate between two square towers at the top of a ramp; the holder's stone gate once restored
the gatehouse of giant blocks astride the switchback road: two bastions, a passage under one monstrous lintel with its relieving triangle, a walk on top at 8 m (Brontes hurls from here)
the gatehouse along y
8 m of cyclopean wall of giant blocks, the walk at 6 m
8 m of cyclopean wall of giant blocks, the walk at 6 m
a round bastion of giant blocks, open fighting top
the oracle shrine: an Ionic naiskos with a red pediment and a ring of six bronze tripod cauldrons that ring in the wind (as at Dodona)
the priestess's house: fieldstone walls, a tiled gable, a timber porch
the Spring of Memory: clear dark water, a stepped basin under a stele with a lion-head spout
the Spring of Lethe: black still water, a cypress-dark stele, a stepped basin under a stele with a lion-head spout
the great anvil (a forge L3+, 4000 hp): a dark iron anvil the size of a cart on a cyclopean plinth, a horn to +x, chains (Gyges is bound here), a hearth basin of coals
the water bellows: an undershot wheel turned by the falls drives a rocking beam over two great leather bellows
the slag heap: glassy black slag and rusty cinder, a few bronze-green runs
a cliffside guard tower over the rock bridge (2 of them): rough cyclopean socle, square shaft, tiled roof
